reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Inspection of unsafe scaffolding and similar devices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 10230; prior revision 1929 § 13273). Directs the director of the inspection section or local building-law enforcement authority, upon notice that scaffolding, platforms, or related parts used on buildings, bridges, or viaducts are unsafe or dangerous to life or limb, to cause an immediate inspection.

headings.title: Notice, prohibition, and repair of dangerous scaffolding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 10230). Covers notifying the responsible person personally or by posting notice when scaffolding or parts are found dangerous, warning against and prohibiting use, and requiring cessation of use, removal, and alteration or strengthening to render the device safe.

headings.title: Inspector access to buildings and premises
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 10230). Grants the director of the inspection section, deputies, or local authorities acting under sections 292.450 to 292.540 free access at all reasonable hours to buildings, structures, or premises containing or using covered scaffolding or devices.

headings.title: Weight-bearing capacity, overloading, and overcrowding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 10230). Requires swinging and stationary scaffolding, platforms, and other devices to bear four times the maximum working weight and prohibits unsafe or dangerous overloading or overcrowding.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 10230; prior revision 1929 § 13273) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked notice-triggered inspection authority (director of inspection section and local building-law authorities), personal/posted unsafe-scaffolding notice and repair duties, reasonable-hours access under sections 292.450 to 292.540, and four-times load capacity plus overloading/overcrowding limits. Revised sub 4 title to cover overcrowding alongside overloading; retained subs 1-3.

headings.title: Commission establishment, membership, terms, vacancies, and removal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al., A.L. 1992 S.B. 480, A.L. 1993 H.B. 550, A.L. 1996 S.B. 740). Establishes the Missouri Emergency Response Commission domiciled in the department of public safety; specifies ex officio directors or designees, six governor-appointed senate-confirmed members with representation and political-party limits, four legislative appointees, staggered four-year terms without term limits, vacancy appointments, and removal for cause.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al., through 1996 S.B. 740). Provides that commission members serve without compensation but are reimbursed for necessary travel and other official expenses.

headings.title: Joint powers and duties of commission and department
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 (including subdivisions (1)-(9)) and source notes. Enumerates joint duties of the commission and department under sections 292.600 to 292.625 and federal EPCRA (P.L. 99-499), including local district/committee designation and review, single filing point, grant administration, technical assistance, department-coordinated training, interagency agreements, section 292.604 fund allotments, and a data management system.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections (including sub 3 subdivisions (1)-(9)) and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al., through A.L. 1996 S.B. 740) and verified all fingerprints. Verified Missouri Emergency Response Commission domicile in DPS, ex officio/gubernatorial/legislative composition, party cap, staggered four-year terms, vacancy and removal-for-cause terms, uncompensated expense reimbursement, and joint commission-department duties under sections 292.600 to 292.625 and federal EPCRA (P.L. 99-499). Retained all 3 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Funding sources for commission and department duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al., A.L. 1992 S.B. 480). Provides that commission and department duties under sections 292.600 to 292.625 are funded by the chemical emergency preparedness fund and general revenue upon appropriation.

headings.title: Distribution and use of appropriated fee revenues
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)(a)-(d), (2), and (3)) and source notes. Allocates section 292.606(2) fees 65% to local emergency planning committees (one-third equally and two-thirds by hazardous-chemical facilities and transport corridors, with transfer to district committees, permitted-use conditions, refusal of future funds, and legal recovery), 25% to commission/department duties, and 10% to the division of fire safety for commission-reviewed hazardous-materials training.

headings.title: Deposit of section 292.606 fees into preparedness fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al., A.L. 1992 S.B. 480). Requires fees collected by the commission under section 292.606 to be placed in the chemical emergency preparedness fund for state and federal-act responsibilities.

headings.title: Administration of donations, grants, contracts, and interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al., A.L. 1992 S.B. 480). Directs the department in conjunction with the commission to administer private donations, federal grants, contracts, accruing fund interest, and other funds for chemical emergency preparedness under sections 292.600 to 292.625 and the federal act.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections (including sub 2 subdivisions (1)(a)-(d), (2), and (3)) and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al., A.L. 1992 S.B. 480) and verified all fingerprints. Checked appropriations qualification in sub 1, 65%/25%/10% distribution of section 292.606(2) fees plus district transfers, permitted-use conditions, refusal/recovery remedies, and fire-safety training review in sub 2, fund deposits in sub 3, and joint administration of donations, grants, contracts, and interest in sub 4. Retained all 4 drafted titles.

headings.title: Employer hazardous-substance reporting and Tier II compliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1985 H.B. 507 & 139 § 2, A.L. 1987 H.B. 655, A.L. 1988 S.B. 765, A.L. 1992 S.B. 480). Requires employers to report hazardous-substance properties and nature to local fire protection services, the department, and local emergency planning committees, and allows satisfaction via annual 40 CFR Part 370 Tier II forms or department-approved alternatives, which also satisfy federal SARA Title III commission reporting.

headings.title: On-site inspections, safety data, and additional hazard disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (1985-1992 amendments). Requires employers to permit fire-chief on-site inspections under federal P.L. 99-499, supply requested MSDS/descriptions/diagrams, disclose section 260.500 hazardous substances posing potential fire/release threats, allows DNR hazardous-waste reports under sections 260.350 to 260.432 to satisfy requirements for those substances, and makes required information publicly available under federal Title III.

headings.title: Emergency contact information on Tier II forms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (1985-1992 amendments). Requires employers to list on the Tier II form the names, current addresses, and telephone numbers of at least two knowledgeable emergency contacts for the department, local emergency planning committee, and local fire protection service.

headings.title: Annual March 1 and changed-condition updates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (1985-1992 amendments). Requires employer information under sections 292.600 to 292.625 to be updated each March 1 or more frequently if changed conditions could affect local fire-response effectiveness.

headings.title: Public access, written requests, request inspection, and fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (1985-1992 amendments). Makes subsection 1 employer information publicly available upon written request, allows affected employers to inspect requests during normal business hours, and authorizes actual-cost fees by the fire service, department, or local committee.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections and source notes (L. 1985 H.B. 507 & 139 § 2 through A.L. 1992 S.B. 480) and verified all fingerprints. Checked 40 CFR Part 370 Tier II and SARA Title III satisfaction in sub 1, fire-chief on-site inspections, MSDS/diagram disclosures, section 260.500 substances, and DNR sections 260.350-260.432 waste report satisfaction in sub 2, emergency contacts in sub 3, March 1/changed-condition updates in sub 4, and public written requests, employer inspection of requests, and actual-cost fees in sub 5. Revised sub 5 title to 'request inspection' to avoid confusion with sub 2 on-site inspections; retained subs 1-4.

headings.title: Six-year fee collection period from August 28, 2025
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1992 S.B. 480 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 71 merged with S.B. 81 & 174). Specifies that fees shall be collected for six years from August 28, 2025; describes archived version text without certifying current enforceability.

headings.title: Annual fees, exemptions, due date, late fees, and credits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)-(4)) and source notes (1992-2025). Covers Tier II annual fees, local-government and family-farm exemptions, petroleum retail cap, federal hazmat fee deductions, product-grouping and facility definitions, per-substance thresholds and $10,000 cap, pipeline per-county fees (excluding PSC-regulated local gas distributors), March 1 due date and discretionary late fees, and proportionate credits when collections plus section 640.235 damages exceed $1 million. Source discrepancy retained: subdivision (4) references "the review of fees as required in subsection 1," though subsection 1 in this 2025 version states only the six-year collection period.

headings.title: Optional commission distribution of Tier II reports and fee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (1992-2025). Beginning January 1, 2013, permits filing employers to pay an additional $10 per facility (deposited in the section 292.607 fund) for the commission to distribute Tier II reports to listed local committees and fire departments, satisfying section 292.605(1) notification if all required recipients are listed.

headings.title: Local committee coordination and annual reporting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (1992-2025). Requires local emergency planning committees receiving section 292.604 funds to coordinate with the commission and department, and requires committees funded under listed sections (260.394, 292.602, 292.604, 292.605, 292.606, 292.615, and 640.235) to submit an annual report of expenditures and activities to the commission.

headings.title: Permitted uses and pooling of preparedness funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (1992-2025). Lists authorized chemical emergency preparedness uses of department fees and local committee funds under sections 292.600 to 292.625 and the federal act, and permits local committees to combine funds with other local committees.

headings.title: Commission criteria and guidance for local fund use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (1992-2025). Directs the commission to establish criteria and guidance on how local emergency planning committees may use received funds.

headings.title: One-time 2025 fee assessment and payment deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (1992-2025, including A.L. 2025 S.B. 71 merged with S.B. 81 & 174). Directs assessment of a one-time fee under subsection 2 calculated from the March 1, 2025 filing and payable by November 1, 2025.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 7 subsections (including sub 2 subdivisions (1)-(4)) and source notes (L. 1992 S.B. 480 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 71 merged with S.B. 81 & 174) and verified all fingerprints. Verified the six-year fee period from August 28, 2025 in sub 1, annual Tier II fees, local-government/family-farm exemptions, petroleum retail cap, federal hazmat fee deduction, $10,000 cap, pipeline fees excluding PSC-regulated local gas distributors, March 1 due date/discretionary late fees, and $1 million credit threshold in sub 2 (retaining the source discrepancy in sub 2(4) cross-referencing 'the review of fees as required in subsection 1' where sub 1 states only the six-year collection period), optional $10 commission distribution in sub 3, local committee coordination/reporting in sub 4, permitted uses/pooling in sub 5, commission guidance in sub 6, and the one-time 2025 fee calculated on March 1, 2025 filings due November 1, 2025 in sub 7. Retained all 7 drafted titles.

headings.title: Fund creation, deposits, interest, and nonreversion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al.). Establishes the Chemical Emergency Preparedness Fund for section 292.604 appropriations, donations, federal grants, contracts, and other funds, retains accruing interest in the fund, and exempts fund balances from reversion to general revenue notwithstanding section 33.080.

headings.title: Appropriated use to implement sections 292.600 to 292.625
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al.). Provides that the chemical emergency preparedness fund shall be used, upon appropriation, to implement sections 292.600 to 292.625.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al.) and verified all fingerprints. Verified Chemical Emergency Preparedness Fund creation, deposit sources referencing section 292.604, retained interest, nonreversion notwithstanding section 33.080 in sub 1, and appropriation-conditioned use for sections 292.600 to 292.625 in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Employer trade secret claims under federal standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1985 H.B. 507 & 139 § 3, A.L. 1988 S.B. 765). Directs that employer trade secret claims be made to the department and protected similarly to Title III, Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know, of federal SARA of 1986 (P.L. 99-499).

headings.title: Prohibited disclosure of protected records and criminal penalty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1985 H.B. 507 & 139 § 3, A.L. 1988 S.B. 765). Prohibits listed public officers, employees, agents, commission members, and committee members/employees from disclosing records protected under sections 292.600 to 292.625 and federal Title III (source text reads "Emergency Response and Community Right-to-Know" rather than "Emergency Planning") until exemption ends or final judicial denial, making violations misuse of official information punishable under section 576.050.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1985 H.B. 507 & 139 § 3, A.L. 1988 S.B. 765) and verified all fingerprints. Verified employer trade-secret claims under federal SARA Title III standards in sub 1 and the nondisclosure bar and section 576.050 misuse-of-official-information penalty in sub 2, retaining the archived source wording discrepancy in sub 2 ('Emergency Response and Community Right-to-Know' vs. 'Emergency Planning' in sub 1). Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Attorney general actions, injunctions, and civil penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1985 H.B. 507 & 139 § 4, A.L. 1987 H.B. 655, A.L. 1988 S.B. 765, A.L. 1992 S.B. 480). Directs the attorney general to bring circuit-court actions against employers knowingly and intentionally violating sections 292.600 to 292.625, granting injunctive jurisdiction and civil penalties (including reasonable attorney fees and costs) up to $5,000 per violation per day, payable to general revenue.

headings.title: Tier II civil actions and listed-section class C misdemeanors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (1985-1992 amendments). Authorizes the commission, local emergency planning committees, or fire protection services (with advance commission approval and cooperation for local committees/fire services) to bring civil actions against employers failing to submit Tier II forms 30 days after noncompliance notice, and designates violations of sections 260.394, 292.602, 292.604, 292.605, 292.606, 292.615, and 640.235 as class C misdemeanors.

headings.title: Civil actions and fund recovery against local committees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (1985-1992 amendments). Authorizes any employer, the department, or the commission to bring a civil action against a local emergency planning committee for failing to use or misusing section 292.604 fees, and allows the department and commission to recover inconsistently spent funds by appropriate legal means.

headings.title: Commission civil action for missing committee reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (1985-1992 amendments). Authorizes the Missouri emergency response commission to commence a civil action against a local emergency planning committee failing to provide information required under section 292.606(4).

headings.title: Investigative access, obstruction prohibition, and search warrants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (1985-1992 amendments). Prohibits refusing entry or obstructing credentialed department representatives investigating possible violations of sections 292.600 to 292.625 or the federal act, and authorizes courts of competent jurisdiction to issue restricted search warrants upon written probable cause under oath.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections and source notes (L. 1985 H.B. 507 & 139 § 4 through A.L. 1992 S.B. 480) and verified all fingerprints. Checked knowing-and-intentional AG enforcement/penalties in sub 1, Tier II civil actions (30-day notice and advance commission approval for local committees/fire services) plus class C misdemeanors for violations of listed sections (260.394, 292.602, 292.604, 292.605, 292.606, 292.615, and 640.235) in sub 2, civil actions/fund recovery against local committees in sub 3, commission action for missing section 292.606(4) reports in sub 4, and credentialed investigative entry/obstruction/search warrants in sub 5. Revised sub 2 title to clarify that class C misdemeanors apply to listed sections rather than only Tier II filings; retained subs 1 and 3-5.

headings.title: Temporary explosive storage reports, fire notices, and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al., A.L. 1990 S.B. 719). Requires section 292.605 reports for temporary storage of 100+ pounds of 49 CFR Part 173 Subpart C explosives/blasting agents for more than 15 days or upon relocation, or 24-hour local fire-department notice for storage of less than 15 days (source text leaves exactly 15 days unstated), while exempting manufacturer/distributor pre-sale storage and DOT-compliant materials in transit.

headings.title: Facility and transport hazard markings and exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al., A.L. 1990 S.B. 719). Requires visible NFPA 704 or federal hazard markings (or optional 29 CFR 1910.1200(f) container markings—source omits "Occupational" before "Safety and Health Administration") on reporting facilities unless exempt via an emergency response policy or local fire protection code, and accepts USDOT markings for motor vehicles, rolling stock, and aircraft.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1989 H.B. 77, et al., A.L. 1990 S.B. 719) and verified all fingerprints. Verified temporary explosive/blasting-agent storage thresholds (100+ lbs, >15 days vs. <15 days 24-hour local fire notice, retaining the exact-15-day statutory gap) and manufacturer/distributor pre-sale and DOT-compliant transit exceptions in sub 1, and NFPA 704/federal hazard markings, emergency-response-policy and local-fire-code exemptions, optional 29 CFR 1910.1200(f) container markings (retaining archived omission of 'Occupational' before 'Safety and Health Administration'), and USDOT transport markings in sub 2. Revised sub 2 title to include exemptions explicitly; retained sub 1.

headings.title: Portable toilet ratio on construction sites and railroad exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1995 S.B. 96 § 2). Requires the primary employer or contractor at construction projects with 20 or more workers to provide at least one portable toilet per 20 people, with an express exception for railroad companies.

headings.title: Division enforcement and section 290.340 willful-violation penalty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1995 S.B. 96 § 2). Assigns enforcement to the department of labor and industrial relations through the division of labor standards and subjects primary employers or contractors found by a court to have willfully violated or omitted compliance to the penalty in section 290.340.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1995 S.B. 96 § 2) and verified all fingerprints. Verified 20-worker threshold, primary employer/contractor duty, railroad company exception in sub 1, and division of labor standards enforcement plus court-found willful-violation penalty under section 290.340 in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: State offer of hepatitis B immunization to at-risk employees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1997 H.B. 635 § 1, subsecs. 1 to 5). Requires Missouri, consistent with CDC public health practices and recommendations, to offer hepatitis B immunization to every state employee determined to be at risk under the federal OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard.

headings.title: Materials for departments to identify at-risk employees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1997 H.B. 635 § 1, subsecs. 1 to 5). Directs the department of health and senior services, with the office of administration division of personnel, to provide materials enabling each state department to identify employees at risk of occupational hepatitis B exposure.

headings.title: Department identification, reporting, and employee educational materials
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1997 H.B. 635 § 1, subsecs. 1 to 5). Requires each state department to identify at-risk employees and report the count to DHSS, and directs DHSS to supply occupational-exposure materials for reporting departments to distribute.

headings.title: Distributing materials and counting vaccination requests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1997 H.B. 635 § 1, subsecs. 1 to 5). Requires each department to distribute DHSS occupational-exposure materials to identified at-risk employees and determine how many request the hepatitis B vaccination.

headings.title: Providing hepatitis B vaccine and administration procedures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1997 H.B. 635 § 1, subsecs. 1 to 5). Requires each department to provide the hepatitis B vaccine to every identified at-risk employee requesting it and to determine administration procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections and source notes (L. 1997 H.B. 635 § 1, subsecs. 1 to 5) and verified all fingerprints. Verified CDC/OSHA bloodborne-pathogens scope for at-risk state employees in sub 1, DHSS and office of administration identification materials in sub 2, department identification, count reporting, and DHSS educational materials in sub 3, distribution and request counting in sub 4, and vaccine provision and administration procedures in sub 5. Retained all 5 drafted titles.

headings.title: Definitions of engineered injury protection device and medical needles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)(a)-(b) and (2)) and source notes (L. 2012 H.B. 1647). Defines "engineered injury protection device" (excluding recapping with original packaging cover) and "medical needles" for purposes of section 292.655.

headings.title: Permitted employer use of injury protection devices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 2012 H.B. 1647). Permits employers routinely using medical needles in Missouri business to use any commercially available engineered injury protection device reasonably expected to reduce accidental needlestick injuries to employees, patients, or customers.

headings.title: Exclusions for animal tools and licensed veterinary care
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 2012 H.B. 1647). Excludes sharp animal-related tools unrelated to live-animal health care or testing (such as skin-sewing needles, fish hooks, gaffs, and animal tags) and veterinary care provided by licensed veterinarians or veterinary care providers within the scope of chapter 340 in or outside a veterinary office.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections (including sub 1 subdivisions (1)(a)-(b) and (2)) and source notes (L. 2012 H.B. 1647) and verified all fingerprints. Verified section-specific definitions (excluding original-cover recapping) in sub 1, permissive ('may use') employer use of commercially available injury protection devices in sub 2, and exclusions for non-healthcare dead-animal/sharp tools and chapter 340 licensed veterinary care in sub 3. Retained all 3 drafted titles.

headings.title: Definitions for public works safety training
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)-(8)) and source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2009 H.B. 390; effective-date note: emergency clause effective 7-07-09 vs. subsection 10 mandate of 8-28-09). Defines construction, contractor, department, on-site employee (including adjacent facilities and excluding sole material/fuel/equipment delivery), person, public body, public works (including certain contracted utility work), and subcontractor.

headings.title: Ten-hour OSHA or equivalent safety training requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (2008-2009 history and dual-effective-date note). Requires public works contractors and subcontractors to provide a 10-hour OSHA-approved or equivalently stringent department-approved construction safety program for on-site employees unless previously completed, with a 60-day completion window from beginning work.

headings.title: Twenty-day grace period to produce training documentation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (2008-2009 history and effective-date note). Affords any on-site employee found without course completion documentation 20 days to produce it before being subject to removal from the project.

headings.title: Contract terms, forfeiture penalties, withholding, and recovery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (2008-2009 history and effective-date note). Requires bid/ordinance and contract specifications and penalty notices, requires contractor/subcontractor compliance, imposes contractor forfeiture penalties ($2,500 plus $100 per untrained employee per calendar day after subsections 2-3 periods elapse), mandates public-body payment withholding, and permits contractor withholding from or circuit-court recovery against at-fault subcontractors.

headings.title: Department violation investigations, notices, and circuit-court appeals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (2008-2009 history and effective-date note). Directs the department of labor and industrial relations to investigate claimed violations, notify the public body and violating parties of findings and penalty assessments, and allows appeals in the circuit court where the public works project is located.

headings.title: Enforcement actions for unpaid penalties and cost recovery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (2008-2009 history and effective-date note). Directs the department to pursue enforcement if a contractor or subcontractor fails to pay an assessed penalty within 45 days after notification, entitling the department to recover actual enforcement costs if the court orders payment.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (2008-2009 history and effective-date note). Authorizes implementing rules under chapter 536 (sections 536.010 and 536.028) and includes a nonseverability clause voiding rulemaking authority and rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2008 if legislative review/annulment powers are held unconstitutional.

headings.title: Exemption for work involving PSC-regulated public utilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 and source notes (2008-2009 history and effective-date note). Exempts work performed by public utilities under public service commission jurisdiction, their contractors, or work performed at or on facilities owned or operated by such utilities.

headings.title: Exemption for certain rail grade crossing improvement projects
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 9 and source notes (2008-2009 history and effective-date note). Exempts rail grade crossing improvement projects covered by a signed agreement between the railroad and MoDOT or a MoDOT construction order.

headings.title: Stated effective date of August 28, 2009
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 10 and source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2009 H.B. 390; Effective 7-07-09). States that the section takes effect August 28, 2009; source footnote keyed to *292.675 explicitly notes an emergency clause making the 2009 amendments effective upon the governor's signature on July 7, 2009 despite subsection 10's August 28, 2009 mandate. Title describes subsection 10's stated date neutrally without resolving the effective-date note.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 10 subsections (including sub 1 subdivisions (1)-(8)) and all source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2009 H.B. 390; Effective 7-07-09; *292.675 footnote contrasting the 7-07-09 emergency clause with subsection 10's 8-28-09 mandate) and verified all fingerprints. Checked sub 1 definitions (including sub 1(7) contracted utility work vs. sub 8 PSC-regulated utility exemption), 10-hour OSHA/equivalent training and 60-day window in sub 2, 20-day documentation grace period in sub 3, contract clauses, forfeiture penalties, withholding, and subcontractor recovery in sub 4, investigations/appeals in sub 5, 45-day enforcement/cost recovery in sub 6, chapter 536 nonseverability voiding post-August 28, 2008 rulemaking if legislative review powers are invalidated in sub 7, PSC utility and MoDOT rail grade crossing exemptions in subs 8-9, and sub 10's August 28, 2009 effective date. Revised sub 10 title to 'Stated effective date of August 28, 2009' for neutrality alongside the dual-effective-date footnote; retained subs 1-9.
